To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new variational Monte Carlo technique for the study of neutron matter that allows us to obtain accurate predictions of the equation of state at densities relevant for the crust-core transition in neutron stars.
we have developed a new approach to the nuclear many-body problem based on the auxiliary-field Monte Carlo method.
the chiral nuclear forces can be used for the study of neutron matter in the framework of the auxiliary-field quantum Monte-Carlo simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of quantum Monte Carlo methods to the description of nuclear systems at zero and nonzero temperature.
the development of a new generation of neutron star models, based on the state-of-the-art chiral effective field theories (EFTs) of low-energy nuclear physics.
the development of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods for the study of many-body problems in physics, chemistry and biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented here, in combination with those from other methods, strongly suggest that neutron matter is a superfluid in a broad range of densities.
the neutron matter calculations are in good agreement with the chiral EFT calculations.
the neutron matter equation-of-state is well reproduced in the density range of 0.02 fm(-3)≤ρ≤0.1 fm(-3) and that the results are in good agreement with other calculations and experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutron matter equation-of-state is well described by the chiral nuclear interaction, and that our results are consistent with the predictions of the many-body theory of neutron matter.
it is the first time that the equation of state of neutron matter has been calculated with a many-body method that is not afflicted with the fermion sign-problem.
it provides a new approach to solving many-body problems, and in particular, to the problem of neutron matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chiral forces are able to describe neutron matter with an accuracy comparable to that obtained in previous variational Monte Carlo studies of neutron matter with phenomenological forces.
chiral nuclear forces, which reproduce the properties of finite nuclei very well, are also capable of reproducing the equation of state of neutron matter.
auxiliary-field quantum Monte-Carlo calculations of nuclear matter can provide a valuable benchmark for ab initio calculations in the continuum.
